sector: Packaging manufacturing / FMCG distribution (glass and plastic bottles)
hitl_conditions: SC managers/stakeholders scrutinize the twin during design, monitoring and evaluation; the planning unit receives forecasts and alternative designs to select strategies; manually entered legacy data is auto-validated and down-weighted (Tier 3-4); some responses (contingency plans, ERP policy updates) run automatically.
key_finding: A three-layer distribution-system twin (physical world, reported data, digital world) with an Elastic Net demand-forecasting core feeding a simulation-optimisation DSS integrated with ERP; in a glass/plastic bottle manufacturer it reports R2 0.86-0.87, MAE 9.2% of mean demand, 85-89% service levels and 22% better forecast accuracy.

quotes.text: Fig. 2 illustrates the three-layer architecture of the proposed digital twin framework for demand prediction. The Physical World layer (bottom) depicts real-world entities like customers and distribution centers, with data collected through IoT sensors and ERP systems.
A real industrial case a company is presented in this section, that manufactures glass and plastic products, established 50 years ago in collaboration with a bank, is examined.
quotes.section: 4. Digital twin conceptualization in a case problem

quotes.text: the predictive core of the proposed digital twin employs scikit-learn's (v1.1.2) ElasticNet regression (α = 0.5, l1_ratio = 0.7) as the primary algorithm, trained on 18 months of historical data from the case study company

Hence, the system automatically triggers increasing production at F2 (shown in Table 3's state change), rerouting shipments from F1 (evident in reduced outflows), and adjusting safety stock parameters (Table 2).

The proposed approach includes fundamental steps such as design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the DT model, in which all main stakeholders, such as supply chain managers, actively participate.

In this final step, the output data is reported to the planning unit, and the results are integrated with existing systems (such as logistics and warehousing units), which are typically managed using ERP systems.
